transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Liam Park (Solace Head of ML), Anita Rao (Eng Manager), Jared Kim (CTO)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Solace is evaluating an embeddings+rerank flow, currently using FAISS for offline embedding store, considering Pinecone for managed vector DB. They have latency SLOs for realtime search (tail 95 < 150ms) and peak QPS around 250-300. Main concerns: cost for high-dim embeddings (1024), vector DB throughput, hybrid search (BM25 + vector) and private deployment options due to data residency.

00:00:06 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone thanks for joining, can you all hear me okay?
00:00:09 Speaker 2 (Liam): Yeah loud and clear, thanks Maya.
00:00:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): Awesome. Quick intros I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, with Diego from our SE team. Over to you, Solace folks?
00:00:18 Speaker 3 (Anita): Hi I'm Anita, engineering manager on search infra.
00:00:20 Speaker 4 (Jared): Jared, CTO.
00:00:22 Speaker 2 (Liam): Liam Park, head of ML.
00:00:25 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great, thanks. The plan today is to understand your current stack, goals for embeddings/rerank, constraints (security, latency, cost), and then go over how Redwood can fit (Hosted / Dedicated / Private). Sound good?
00:00:35 Speaker 3 (Anita): Yup, sounds good.

00:01:02 Speaker 2 (Diego): To kick off, could you give us a quick overview of your current retrieval pipeline indexing cadence, which embedding model you use, vector DB, and typical QPS?
00:01:12 Speaker 2 (Liam): Sure. Right now we embed with a custom fine-tuned 768-d model (based on SBERT). Our online store is FAISS running on Kubernetes nodes; it's mostly CPU with some GPU during batch re-index. For production search we do BM25 candidate generation then vector rerank on top-200 candidates. Peak QPS is around 250, average 60. Latency SLO for user-facing search is p95 under 150ms, ideally 100. We also have nightly full re-index.
00:01:40 Speaker 2 (Diego): Are you doing approximate NN (HNSW) on FAISS?
00:01:42 Speaker 2 (Liam): Yes HNSW for ANN. Quality is okay but the ops cost is mounting and we want a managed option. Also exploring larger embedding dims 128 vs 768 vs 1024 tradeoffs are confusing.

00:02:22 Speaker 1 (Maya): Understood. Two quick clarifying q's: would you consider a managed vector DB like Pinecone, or do you need self-hosted because of compliance? And what's your expected growth over the next 12 months?
00:02:35 Speaker 2 (Liam): We prefer managed for dev velocity but for a subset of clients we need VPC/private deployment due to data residency and contracts. Growth  all expect to double QPS to ~500 in 12 months for a new product launch.

00:03:05 Speaker 2 (Diego): Thanks. A couple of notes from Redwood side  we support hosted endpoints (fastest), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for stricter compliance. For embeddings pipelines we can host the embedding model and produce vectors, or you can bring-your-own embeddings and just use our reranker + serving. Which model do you plan to standardize on?
00:03:26 Speaker 2 (Liam): We're considering staying on our tuned 768 but benchmarking against open-source 1024-d models for better semantic recall. Main worry is cost and index size if we go to 1024-d.

00:04:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): Makes sense. On dimensionality higher dims typically increase embedding size linearly (and storage & bandwidth). For vector DBs that can affect both latency and cost. We usually recommend experimenting with lower-d projections (PCA/OPQ) or quantization to reduce footprint, but it depends on your retrieval quality targets.
00:04:34 Speaker 3 (Anita): Do you support PQ/OPQ or quantized tensors on your side?
00:04:38 Speaker 2 (Diego): We have quantization-friendly paths in the runtime and can recommend quant profiles. For Hosted we offer managed quantization options; for Dedicated you can pick specific kernels and FP16/INT8 quant flows. For Private we'd advise a quantization plan during onboarding.

00:05:01 Speaker 4 (Jared): We're also concerned about reranker latency when you said Hosted vs Dedicated, how would latency look for a two-stage pipeline (vector candidate gen + model rerank)?
00:05:12 Speaker 2 (Diego): Good q. Typical pattern: candidate retrieval from vector DB (either a managed service or our local KNN in Dedicated) takes ~10-40ms depending on dim and shards; then rerank with a small cross-encoder or lightweight MLP can add 20-120ms depending on model size. With our Dedicated capacity you can get stable p95s under 100ms for the reranker for small models. For Hosted endpoints numbers vary by plan; we expose perf profiles per model.

00:06:00 Speaker 2 (Liam): Are we able to run the reranker colocated with the vector DB to avoid network hops? That's been a big perf win for us with FAISS colocated.
00:06:08 Speaker 2 (Diego): Yes on Dedicated and Private you can colocate compute to minimize network latency. For Hosted we have region-affinity and low-latency routes, but it's not the same as co-locating in customer VPC.

00:06:33 Speaker 1 (Maya): Quick aside  do you have any security/compliance gating items, e.g., SOC2, SSO, or encryption requirements?
00:06:40 Speaker 3 (Anita): SOC2 is required, SAML SSO for internal users, and for some customers we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs. Also data residency for EU customers.
00:06:51 Speaker 1 (Maya): Redwood supports SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integrations, and audit logging. Private deployments can meet data residency/KMS constraints. We'll share our security pack after the call.

00:07:15 Speaker 2 (Liam): Can you run through integration patterns? Do you ingest embeddings into your hosted vector store or do you push from our infra?
00:07:24 Speaker 2 (Diego): We support several flows: 1) Redwood-managed embeddings + vector store: we host the embedding model, produce vectors, and store them in our managed vector DB; 2) BYO embeddings push to Redwood's store (we accept raw vectors via API); 3) Connectors to third-party vector DBs (e.g., Pinecone) where Redwood calls out to the store and handles rerank in our runtime. We can also support hybrid search where BM25 runs in your infra and we do rerank.

00:07:52 Speaker 2 (Liam): If we keep FAISS in our cluster but want Redwood reranker, what's the flow latency-wise?
00:07:58 Speaker 2 (Diego): You'd do candidate gen in your cluster, send top-k candidates to Redwood rerank endpoint payload size is small if you send ids and lightweight features; reranker runs and returns scores. That round trip depends on network but often ~30-80ms. For lowest latency, colocating or Dedicated Xavier will be best.

00:08:34 Speaker 4 (Jared): We're also thinking about hybrid retrieval BM25 for lexical matches and vectors for semantic. Any guidance on how to combine and weight?
00:08:42 Speaker 2 (Diego): Common approach: generate candidates from BM25 and ANN, merge & dedupe, then rerank with a cross-encoder that takes both query + doc text and optionally vector features. Another variant is rank fusion score normalize BM25 and vector cosine then linear combine. We can help run evaluation on your labeled queries to pick weights or train a learned reranker.

00:09:12 Speaker 2 (Liam): How do you handle scaling for peak QPS? If we hit 500 QPS with rerank on top-200 candidates, that seems enormous gas cost-wise.
00:09:22 Speaker 2 (Diego): Reranking top-200 at 500 QPS is heavy; usual optimizations: reduce candidates to top-50, use a two-tier rerank (fast lightweight model then a more expensive cross-encoder for top-5), or cache results for repeated queries. Redwood's Optimize tooling can recommend batching and cache policies; Dedicated capacity gives predictable throughput so you can right-size. Also consider using smaller embeddings for initial recall then high-dim for rerank.

00:10:03 Speaker 3 (Anita): Do you expose token or request-level cost estimates? Our finance team will want to model the cost per query for different architectures.
00:10:11 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes our pricing model for Hosted is usage-based (per-embedding unit and per-rerank request). For Dedicated it's capacity commitments. We'll send an example cost model spreadsheet comparing top-50 vs top-200 rerank scenarios.

00:10:35 Speaker 2 (Liam): For vector dimensionality, do you have recommended sweet spots? We've seen 128 dims work well for some tasks, but for our domain 768/1024 might matter.
00:10:45 Speaker 2 (Diego): It depends on task. Many customers start with 256-768. 1024 can help in niche long-tail semantics but increases storage and ANN latency. We suggest A/B testing with your eval set sometimes quantized 1024 performs similar to 768 full-precision. We'll help run a sweep.

00:11:18 Speaker 4 (Jared): Let's talk about monitoring how observability looks when things go wrong.
00:11:24 Speaker 1 (Maya): Redwood Console has per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost and latency breakdowns, tracing hooks, and error analysis. For Dedicated/Private you can forward tracing data to your observability stack or use our console.

00:11:43 Speaker 2 (Diego): We'll also instrument candidate generation and rerank latency. You can set alerts for p95/p99 regressions and quality regressions tied to eval prompts.

00:12:05 Speaker 2 (Liam): Any customers using Redwood with Milvus or Milvus-based stacks? We're looking at that for on-prem.
00:12:12 Speaker 2 (Diego): A few integrations are straightforward via connectors or gRPC. For Private deployments we can deploy adapters that talk natively to Milvus or your FAISS instances.

00:12:42 Speaker 3 (Anita): On the ops side, how much work is onboarding for Private? We have strict network segmentation.
00:12:48 Speaker 2 (Diego): Private onboarding typically includes a planning call, network runbook, and an install package. If on-prem, we provide container manifests and a support tech during install. Timeline is ~3-6 weeks depending on complexity.

00:13:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): Quick check are there any must-have features that would block a deal?
00:13:15 Speaker 2 (Liam): KMS integration for keys, audit logs, and the ability to keep EU data in-region are blockers for some contracts. Also predictable p95 latency under dedicated capacity.

00:13:34 Speaker 1 (Maya): Noted. We'll include KMS and audit log info in the security pack.

00:13:50 Speaker 2 (Liam): On evaluation we want to run a small POC: push a 10k doc sample, run both 768 and 1024 models for embeddings, run hybrid retrieval on top-50, compare recall and latency. Possible?
00:14:02 Speaker 2 (Diego): Totally. For POC we can spin up a Dedicated trial or use Hosted with higher quota. We'll provide scripts for ingestion and per-query benchmarks and help configure the reranker.

00:14:23 Speaker 4 (Jared): What would you recommend for initial candidate set size? 200 feels safe but heavy.
00:14:29 Speaker 2 (Diego): Start with 100, measure recall. Often 50-100 hits a good quality/latency sweet spot. Use staged rerank for heavy queries.

00:14:52 Speaker 3 (Anita): About vector DB integration  if we use Pinecone for hosting, is there any extra latency when Redwood calls out?
00:14:58 Speaker 2 (Diego): There's a network hop; typically pinecone retrieval is 15-40ms depending on vector dim and region. We do have connectors that batch requests efficiently, but colocation still beats cross-service calls.

00:15:22 Speaker 2 (Liam): Any limitations on embedding size for uploads?
00:15:26 Speaker 2 (Diego): We accept up to 2048-d vectors via API; storage & throughput cost scales accordingly. For very large vectors we recommend quantization or reducing dim.

00:15:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): I'm going to share a quick architecture sketch. (screen share noise) Sorry if transcription garbles the diagram there's a BM25 index, ANN store, Redwood reranker, optional Dedicated pool.
00:15:58 Speaker 3 (Anita): Looks familiar.

00:16:22 Speaker 2 (Diego): A note on batching: for throughput testing we simulate concurrent queries with batch sizes tuned based on average sequence length. Batching can improve GPU utilization but sometimes adds latency for single requests. We can help pick a batch policy.

00:16:48 Speaker 2 (Liam): How do you measure quality are you supporting our labeled eval set to produce AUC/ndcg metrics?
00:16:53 Speaker 2 (Diego): Yes we can run your eval set through candidate gen + rerank and produce recall@k, nDCG, and latency breakdowns. We also support human eval hooks for blind testing.

00:17:18 Speaker 4 (Jared): Pricing sensitivity do you have examples of cost for reranking top-50 at 500 QPS vs 100 QPS?
00:17:26 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll include a model in the spreadsheet but rough ballpark: cost scales with throughput and model compute. Dedicated typically lowers per-request cost at scale vs Hosted. We'll run numbers for your topologies.

00:17:50 Speaker 3 (Anita): Any pitfalls you've seen customers run into?
00:17:55 Speaker 2 (Diego): Three common ones: 1) over-indexing (too large dim without testing); 2) reranking too many candidates; 3) not instrumenting quality regressions after model or prompt changes. We help mitigate with Optimize recommendations and rollout controls.

00:18:20 Speaker 2 (Liam): For the reranker model do you provide prebuilt cross-encoders or do we bring ours?
00:18:27 Speaker 2 (Diego): Both. Redwood has prebuilt smaller cross-encoders we can host, or you can bring a custom model or weights. Dedicated gives more flexibility for custom kernel selection.

00:18:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): Any regulatory questions or region-specific constraints?
00:18:53 Speaker 3 (Anita): GDPR and EU data residency for some enterprise clients.
00:18:58 Speaker 1 (Maya): Private deployments or region-restricted Hosted can address that. We'll note this in the security pack.

00:19:20 Speaker 2 (Diego): Quick technical question are you using dense vector-only rerank or do you also send textual context to the reranker?
00:19:28 Speaker 2 (Liam): We typically send top candidate text snippets plus some metadata; sending full doc can be heavy.
00:19:34 Speaker 2 (Diego): Makes sense. Cross-encoders commonly use truncated context or salient passages. Also consider prioritized fields.

00:19:50 Speaker 4 (Jared): For the POC, what would be the recommended test plan?
00:19:55 Speaker 2 (Diego): 1) Solace provides 10k sample docs + labeled queries. 2) Run embeddings for 768 and 1024, index both. 3) Run hybrid retrieval (BM25 + ANN) with top-50 and top-100 configs. 4) Measure recall/ndcg and latency. 5) Run throughput test to 500 QPS (gradually) on Dedicated trial or Hosted with quota. Diego would own the benchmark scripts and results.

00:20:31 Speaker 3 (Anita): How long does an ingestion and index take for 10k docs?
00:20:35 Speaker 2 (Diego): Usually minutes if parallelized; depends on embedding time per doc. With a hosted embedding model you can do it in under an hour.

00:20:52 Speaker 2 (Liam): Any specific logging or privacy notes when sending data?
00:20:57 Speaker 1 (Maya): For Hosted we log minimal request metadata; we can offer data retention policies. For Dedicated/Private customer data never leaves your tenancy. We'll include the data handling excerpt in the security pack.

00:21:18 Speaker 4 (Jared): Are there SLA guarantees on p95 latency?
00:21:22 Speaker 1 (Maya): SLA-backed latency targets are part of Dedicated enterprise contracts. Hosted has best-effort perf profiles but not the same SLA.

00:21:42 Speaker 2 (Diego): Also worth noting fallback behavior if a model or capacity issue occurs we can route to a cheaper or smaller model to keep availability. That's configurable in rollout policies.

00:21:55 Speaker 2 (Liam): For hybrid search when merging BM25 and vector results, do you have tooling for weight tuning?
00:22:01 Speaker 2 (Diego): Yes we provide tooling for offline grid search on your eval set, and can run automatic sweep to pick weights that maximize nDCG.

00:22:20 Speaker 3 (Anita): Do you support incremental indexing or near-real-time updates? We have frequent document churn.
00:22:26 Speaker 2 (Diego): Yes our pipeline supports incremental updates and delta indexing. For high-churn datasets we recommend micro-batching.

00:22:44 Speaker 1 (Maya): We're at about 22 minutes in; maybe quick pause any burning questions?
00:22:50 Speaker 2 (Liam): One: if we go with Dedicated, what's the onboarding timeline?
00:22:54 Speaker 2 (Diego): For Dedicated it's typically 2-4 weeks for initial provisioning and a bit longer for optimizations and can be accelerated for higher-priority customers.
00:23:06 Speaker 1 (Maya): Another admin I'll send the security pack, pricing sheet, and POC plan after the call.

00:23:18 Speaker 4 (Jared): About cost do you have examples where customers reduced cost by switching to quantization?
00:23:24 Speaker 2 (Diego): Yes some customers saw 30-50% storage/throughput savings with INT8 quant and minimal quality loss after tuning. We'll share anonymized case studies.

00:23:42 Speaker 3 (Anita): Any constraints for bringing our own cross-encoder weights?
00:23:47 Speaker 2 (Diego): We support custom model artifacts; for Hosted there are sandboxed constraints; Dedicated/Private gives more freedom. We do a compatibility check and may suggest kernel tweaks.
00:24:04 Speaker 2 (Liam): For reranker throughput if we serve a small distil cross-encoder, what's realistic per-GPU throughput?
00:24:12 Speaker 2 (Diego): Distil-style cross-encoders can do thousands of inferences per second with batching on a T4/RTX-class GPU. Exact numbers depend on input length and batch policy; we'll load-test for your shapes.
00:24:33 Speaker 1 (Maya): Any more questions before we move to recap?
00:24:36 Speaker 3 (Anita): One quick: do you have built-in A/B rollouts for model changes?
00:24:40 Speaker 2 (Diego): Yes Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic rollback based on latency or quality regressions.
00:24:52 Speaker 2 (Liam): Good.

00:25:08 Speaker 1 (Maya): Recap: Solace wants to evaluate embeddings at 768 vs 1024, run hybrid retrieval with top-50/100, measure latency and quality, and test throughput up to 500 QPS. Blockers: KMS, audit logging, EU data residency. Next steps: Maya sends security pack and pricing; Diego shares benchmark scripts and POC plan; Solace provides 10k sample and targets.
00:25:36 Speaker 4 (Jared): That captures it.
00:25:40 Speaker 3 (Anita): Will you include a sample curl ingestion and rerank call?
00:25:44 Speaker 2 (Diego): Yes, we'll attach sample ingestion scripts and rerank API examples.

00:26:01 Speaker 1 (Maya): Any final comments?
00:26:04 Speaker 2 (Liam): No, thanks everyone. Looking forward to the POC.
00:26:08 Speaker 4 (Jared): Thanks.
00:26:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great, we'll follow up via email with materials.
00:26:16 Speaker 2 (Diego): Thanks all.

(Transcript continues with short QA and wrap: filler and small clarifications)

00:31:05 Speaker 3 (Anita): One more what's your recommended approach for duplicate handling when we merge BM25 and ANN candidate lists?
00:31:13 Speaker 2 (Diego): De-dup by doc-id then prefer higher BM25 score if lexical match exact; otherwise prefer vector score, but reorder with a learned reranker if you have labels.

00:35:42 Speaker 2 (Liam): Slight disclosure we currently use internal caching at the edge for repeated queries, will Redwood's cache interact with that?
00:35:48 Speaker 2 (Diego): Yes caching can be layered. We expose cache controls and TTLs so you can align with edge caching.

00:40:01 Speaker 1 (Maya): wrapping up again we'll send follow-ups and schedule the deep-dive. Thanks everyone.

00:47:58 System: Meeting ended

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-typed product names and may swap Redwood product names (e.g., Reedwood) in the auto transcript. Attachments referenced: security_pack_link (shared via email), pricing_sheet_link, poc_plan_link, sample_ingest_scripts.zip.
